findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type, allowing anonymous denials to poison renderer checks
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey is built only from namespace, checkReq.UserUID, action, name and parent, and Check consults it before dispatching on IdentityType. Anonymous subjects (anonymous:0) and renderer subjects (render:0) both parse to UserUID "0", so an anonymous Check for dashboards:read on dash1 that is denied writes a denial entry under UID 0, and a subsequent render:0 Check for the same namespace/action/name/parent hits that entry at line 117 and returns Allowed:false without ever reaching getRendererPermissions, which is supposed to allow renderers to read all dashboards/folders. The same collision applies between user and service-account subjects sharing a UID string. The key must include the identity type (or the denial cache must not be applied to renderer/anonymous identities).

findings.title: Denial cache key uses ambiguous underscore concatenation, allowing cross-resource collisions
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates userUID, action, name and parent with '_' separators and no escaping or length prefixing. Dashboard/folder UIDs can contain underscores, so distinct tuples collide, e.g. (name="a_b", parent="c") and (name="a", parent="b_c") produce the same key, as do userUID/action boundary variants. A denial legitimately cached for one resource therefore returns Allowed:false for a different resource the user may actually have access to. Encode the components unambiguously (e.g. hash the tuple or use a separator that cannot appear and length-prefix fields).

findings.title: Negative caching reintroduces stale denials for newly granted/created resources
findings.body: After the new DB re-query, any !allowed result is cached in permDenialCache for shortCacheTTL (30s) and subsequent Checks short-circuit at line 117 without re-querying. If a user (or UI) checks a dashboard/folder before its permission row exists or before an admin grants access, and the grant/creation then happens, the creator/grantee is still denied for up to 30s - the exact stale-denial symptom this PR aims to fix for newly created dashboards/folders. It is also set when checkPermission failed only because the folder tree came from the still-cached folderCache (buildFolderTree is not refreshed on the DB fallback), so a stale tree produces a persistent 30s denial even after permissions are re-fetched.

findings.title: List still trusts stale cached permissions with no freshness fallback
findings.body: Unlike Check, which now falls back to getIdentityPermissions when cached permissions do not allow the requested resource, List at line 180 returns whatever getCachedIdentityPermissions returns (permissionCacheUsage hit) and never re-queries the DB. After a user creates or is granted a dashboard/folder, List - the API used to fetch visible resources - will omit the new resource until permCache expires (30s), so the PR's goal of letting creators fetch newly created dashboards/folders is not achieved for listing even though single-resource Check now works.
